productTitle: Bodum 34oz Chambord French Press Coffee Maker, High-Heat Borosilicate Glass, Polished Stainless Steel – Made in Portugal
text: I have had the Bodum Chambord French Press Coffee Maker for about a week. The coffee is perfect everyday. You must have patience. I followed what others were saying about making French Press Coffee on utube and here: freshly ground coarse coffee beans. I make 16 ounces of coffee everyday which fills an 11oz mug. I boil the water then place it off boil for about a minute or two. I then pour 4oz hot water onto the grounds (4 scoops of coffee) and let that sit for a minute or two. Stir gently with a wooden spoon. I then pour the rest of the hot water (12oz) onto the grounds, place the top on the glass container and time it for 4 minutes. While the 4 minutes are brewing the coffee, I take my mug and fill it with water. I microwave that on high for 2 mintues to heat the mug up. When that's done, I place a spoon inside to heat the spoon up. When the 4 minutes are up, I slowly and gently press the filter down the glass container, then slowly over the beans. The coffee is now ready to pour. I dump out the hot water from the mug and immediately pour the coffee in. I never get grounds in my coffee mug b/c the coarse grounds are too big to slip past the filter. It is a perfectly hot cup of coffee everyday but again, achieving that perfection takes patience. Worth every sip! Also, some reviewers were concerned that the glass was fragile and some reviewers broke theirs. I make sure when cleaning the glass and also the filter to be gentle with it and I NEVER put the parts into the dishwasher. Udate: I have had the Bodum, Chambord Press Coffee Maker for a few weeks now. I have followed exactly what I wrote above and I have not had any issues with the glass breaking - because the coffee is worth it, I'm pretty gentle with it when handwashing. Even the filter - I hand wash that as well. Not a big deal for me b/c that coffee is worth every sip! Let me give a s/o to Jim's Coffee in Massachusetts. This is the only coffee I use now and I order from Jim's site itself. I buy whole beans then bring it to the supermarker where I grind the bean on COARSE. I just ordered some decaf and that should be arriving anyday now.
date: Reviewed in the United States on July 9, 2026
title: Patience is worth every sip!
